rules.title: Providence ban on rent-setting algorithms
rules.requirement: Prohibits the use of rent-setting algorithms and algorithmic rent-setting devices. The city solicitor may bring enforcement actions. Violations carry civil penalties, plus costs and attorney fees in a successful enforcement action.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $500 per day per violation, plus costs and attorney fees

coverage.summary: The captured secondary source states no building, unit-count or landlord-size limits. Coverage cannot be confirmed without the ordinance text.

rules.effective_date_note: The only source (a law-firm alert) gives 'effective May 2025' (month only). No exact day or enactment date is captured. The rule is in force as of the 2026-10-01 query date.
citation_aliases: Providence Code of Ordinances ch. 13, art. X, §§ 13-69–13-73
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits the use of rent-setting algorithms; the city expressly linked the measure to software such as RealPage
rules.review_note: Supported only by a secondary source (Morgan Lewis alert, Aug. 21, 2026); no official ordinance text is captured. The following still need checking against the ordinance: definitions of a covered algorithm or device, any exemptions, the enactment date and the exact effective date. The alert notes that such first-of-their-kind ordinances may face challenges to municipal authority. The ordinance is at issue in City of Providence v. Audubon Capital Partners, LLC (Providence Mun. Ct.).
rules.source_notes: Law-firm alert. Penalty and enforcement details are attributed to Providence Code §§ 13-71 & 13-72. The alert's reference to pending regulation in 'Rhode Island' concerns state-level action and is outside this jurisdiction.

also_supported_by.quoted_span: The ordinance authorizes the city solicitor to bring enforcement actions and provides for civil penalties of up to $500 per day per violation, as well as costs and attorney fees in a successful enforcement action.
